summary: Buildable: no errors, all spec examples pass, no blocking open questions. Before the build is final, the PO must decide four major refinement questions: post-submission edits, the late certificate of residence, how non-return days are counted, and the permit reminder for Swiss people living abroad. Six technical or UI leaks should be removed from feature.md. Some rule rows and ACs (AC-07.2.1, AC-08.1.2) rely on fact ids missing from their own citations or say more than the sources do. Fund-dependent questions and the inferred tariff rows remain go-live conditions.

findings.title: No rule for changing answers after submission
findings.why: Only the first working day (AC-02.1.4) is covered. A move, marriage or new child could leave the source-tax status, tariff code, canton and fund civil status wrong, and engineering cannot design editing or recalculation without this.
findings.action: Add a decision to decisions.yaml: which answers stay editable after submission and by whom (employee or HR), and whether derived results are recalculated the way AC-02.2.4 does for the insurance start date.

findings.title: A certificate handed in later leaves the recorded tariff wrong
findings.why: Answering 'not yet' records C1Y. Nobody updates it to N1Y when the certificate arrives, because the HR side is out of scope.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major); US-07.2, AC-07.2.4 'Certificate not yet provided'
findings.action: Decide who updates the answer later and whether the tariff code is recalculated, or accept the risk explicitly and add it to the exclusions.

findings.title: Non-return day limits are unclear for mid-year starters
findings.why: The 60-day (Germany) and 45-day (Liechtenstein) limits are 'per calendar year'. Whether the year is full, remaining or pro-rated changes the tariff and the Liechtenstein result.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement (major); US-07.2, US-07.3; calculator questions C-Q26/C-Q28
findings.action: Ask a domain expert or the Zurich tax office, then record the counting rule in decisions.yaml.

findings.title: Permit reminder also goes to Swiss citizens living abroad
findings.why: Nationality is not asked of people living abroad, so Swiss commuters like Stefan get a reminder that does not apply to them. This interacts with OQ-nationality-scope.
findings.action: Decide together with OQ-nationality-scope: either accept the generic reminder or ask everyone 'Swiss citizen yes/no'.

findings.title: Technical and UI choices in the spec text
findings.why: Internal ids and UI patterns tie engineering to choices no source requires. 'English country names' has no source at all.
findings.evidence: tech_leak x6: 'Kept id permit_type for stability', rule ids pension_fund_civil_status / source_tax_civil_status / source_tax_residence in the text, date entry as DD.MM.YYYY, 'add and remove children', 'country given by its English name'; trace_judge on US-04.1, US-04.2, spouse_nationality, spouse_residence_country
findings.action: Replace rule ids with rule names and delete the permit_type note. State the business need instead of the UI: every child is described, and the fund receives the start date as DD.MM.YYYY. Drop 'English name' or move it into a decision with an owner (see the country-list question).

findings.title: Acceptance criteria say more than their sources
findings.why: Testers will check behaviour that no source supports.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: US-07.2 (AC-07.2.1 'Germany always makes them subject', liability fact not cited); US-08.1 (AC-08.1.2 'handed in person, nothing uploaded' beyond D-010); item.address_country (D-010 not cited)
findings.action: Cite F-hr_transcript-b6d9b3 and D-010 where they apply, or reduce AC-08.1.2 to what the sources say. If upload is out of scope, record that in decisions.yaml.

findings.title: Rule rows rely on fact ids missing from their own citations
findings.why: Traceability is broken for the Germany/Liechtenstein, 'not subject' and H-tariff branches. The core residence rule also adds the assumption that 'home address country' is the test for living abroad.
findings.evidence: trace_judge: source_tax_residence (31d762, e22d17), single_parent_h_tariff (c78e0c), cross_border_tariff_applies (52b67a), liechtenstein_no_source_tax_in_principle (e22d17), source_tax_result (b6d9b3); H-tariff purposes on has_children, child_parental_custody, child_main_financial_contributor; fact_judge F-hr_transcript-b6d9b3
findings.action: Add the missing facts to each rule's citations and back the H-tariff purposes with a calculator fact. Confirm with HR that 'home address country' is the test for living abroad and record it as a decision.

findings.title: Inferred tariff paths still need checking against the calculator
findings.why: Lonio now produces the tariff code itself (D-001). The inferred child rows, more than 3 children, H3N/P3N and the residence block for A/B/H are unverified. The single child digit also has no rule for 10 or more children.
findings.evidence: OQ-calculator-coverage; inferred rows in AC-06.2.3–AC-06.5.3; dev_refinement on child count; fact_judge partial on 3058a4 (garbled statement), 38dd4a, c2faa7, 56e79b, 50f74a
findings.action: Keep the go-live condition: a domain expert compares the computed codes with the calculator. Fix the garbled F-zh_source_tax_calculator-3058a4 and decide on a maximum or display rule for the child digit.

findings.title: Example tables contradict their own criteria
findings.why: The examples pass the simulation, but engineering cannot use them as reliable test cases.
findings.evidence: dev_refinement: AC-01.1.1 (names shown as 'asked' instead of 'required'), AC-05.7.2 (M0N/P1Y rows show '–'), AC-01.3.2 (Italy canton '–'), AC-02.2.4 (Julia example has no change)
findings.action: Correct the tables. Add a second row to the Julia example that shows the start date being moved.

findings.title: Fund-side registration questions are still open
findings.why: These do not block the build, but cross-border employees, registered partners and separated, divorced or widowed employees may be registered wrongly. Dissolved partnerships are also missing from the civil-status list.
findings.evidence: OQ-canton-abroad, OQ-civil-status-partnership, OQ-spouse-dob-other-status; dev_refinement on civil statuses; fact_judge F-pension_portal-6d3630
findings.action: Ask Pensionskasse Muster to confirm the canton for employees abroad and the civil-status mapping, and to send screenshots for Divorced and Widowed. Decide how dissolved partnerships and a deceased partner are mapped.
